summary: End-to-end verification of three new frontend features (chart-overlay/multi-horizon, alert history, share-card localization) and a backend re-verify of the free-credits flow. Backend: all 9 free-credits tests + 4 new wallet-sanity tests PASS (balance shape, enforcement flip when free=0, credit spent on real run and NOT on cache hit, admin bypass never spends). Frontend: OTP login flow works; on a cached AAPL analysis the MULTI-HORIZON tabs correctly change both the card body (thesis + confidence + target/stop levels) AND the chart header label ("LEVELS · 1-2 WEEKS" -> "1-3 MONTHS" -> "6-12 MONTHS" and "CHART · <HORIZON> LEVELS"); chart-mode toggle switches to TradingView and exposes tv-range-1D/1W/1M/1Y chips as expected. Alerts tab has both alerts-tab-active and alerts-tab-history segmented controls; empty states render ("NO ALERTS SET" and "NO FIRED ALERTS YET"); testIDs for clear-triggered and clear-history are wired up. Share-card modal renders correctly localized labels for en/hi/es (all 5 keys under share.* verified) while BUY/SELL/HOLD stays English by design (verdict.buy/sell/hold pinned to English in every locale JSON).

react_native_issues.issue: Repeated pageerror at boot: 'Invalid language tag: en-US@posix'. Comes from the runtime locale detector (expo-localization / i18next) being fed the POSIX locale that Kubernetes containers report. Not fatal (app renders and translations work) but pollutes the console and could break Intl.DateTimeFormat on stricter engines. Reference: src/i18n/* + the locale-detector wiring in src/i18n/index.ts (or wherever expo-localization is read). Sanitize the tag to 'en-US' before feeding i18n.

action_items: (low) Strip the '@posix' suffix (or map en-US@posix -> en-US) before initializing i18next / Intl to silence the boot-time pageerror.

(info, not blocking) End-to-end fire-alert scenario (bell tap -> price cross -> HISTORY row) was not exercised in the browser: RN AsyncStorage on web is IndexedDB-backed so a localStorage inject didn't seed the alerts store, and the current live AAPL quote didn't cross any offered TARGET/STOP level within polling. Store logic (evaluate() -> saveHistory) is straightforward and its unit surface is covered by the empty-state + tab-switch UI checks. Recommend adding a lightweight React Testing Library test around AlertsProvider.evaluate to lock the history-append + persistence invariants.
critical_code_review_comments: analysis/[id].tsx TvSection uses `!widgetChart || showLevels` to decide `ownChart`; if a symbol is not widget-supported (widgetChart=false) the levels/tradingview toggle bar is hidden but the range chips are also hidden because `!ownChart` is false. That looks correct today (own OHLC chart is always shown for non-widget symbols) but tightly couples two independent concerns — consider naming the boolean and adding a comment.

alerts.tsx evaluate() persists via save + saveHistory which are async but never awaited inside setState. If the user backgrounds the app instantly after a fire the write could be lost. Not a regression from this session but worth flagging.

ShareCard uses new Date().toLocaleDateString(i18n.language || 'en', ...). Passing a nullish language falls back to system locale which is what caused the en-US@posix warning on web. Consider pinning to a whitelist of known BCP-47 tags.
seed_data_creation: None. Tests use disposable users minted through auth_helper and delete cached analyses for the specific symbols under test (IBM, INTC).
context_for_next_testing_agent: AUTH_DEBUG_RETURN_OTP was flipped to true for the run and restored to false at the end (verified via /api/auth/otp/request no longer returning debug_otp). Backend supervisor restart done. Cached AAPL analysis with all three horizons + timeframes was relied on for the frontend flow, so the test is fast and deterministic on repeat runs. If IBM/INTC cached analyses interfere with the new pytest, tests already delete them upfront.
rca_of_issue: No new bugs found in this session. The previously reported free-credits concurrency flakiness (root cause: cached analyses skipping the credit spend) stays fixed — the deletion step is present in tests/test_free_credits.py and mirrored here in test_wallet_sanity_iter12.py.
